boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rich Mountain record (July 11, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. The July 6-10 advance, Pegram's attempted escape and surrender on July 13, Garnett's retreat from Laurel Hill and the action at Corrick's Ford are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Nicolay gives Pegram a regiment and six guns in the pass, Garnett three or four regiments at Laurel Hill, McClellan some seven regiments, Rosecrans's turning column portions of four regiments or 1,900 men, and Pegram's detachment at Hart's 310 men and two guns. Pegram says the detachment was about 310 men with one piece, attacked by 3,000; in his addendum his whole force was about 1,300, not more than 350 engaged, against nearly 10,000 in all and 3,000 at Hart's.
claims.rationale: Figures differ in population and between the history and the report (1,900 against 3,000; one gun against two). None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.rationale: Ground from an interested report and a history; no map inspected.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Lieutenant Colonel John Pegram and Brigadier General Robert S. Garnett for the Confederates and Major General George B. McClellan and Brigadier General William S. Rosecrans for the Union; the live page lists McClellan and Pegram. Nicolay says Rosecrans proposed the turning plan and McClellan permitted it, reportedly with some reluctance; Pegram placed De Lagnel at Hart's, led reinforcements himself, and called councils of war before the escape and the surrender. Garnett held Laurel Hill, some seventeen miles north, and no inspected passage places him at Rich Mountain.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report. The four listed commanders do not receive automatic credit; Garnett's listing reflects the wider operation.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says a sharp two-hour fight split the Confederates, half escaping to Beverly while Pegram and the rest surrendered on July 13; Pegram says his detachment held for three hours against ten times its number; Nicolay says the Union numbers quickly decided the contest and that Pegram surrendered 560 men and thirty-three officers.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The duration differs (two hours against three); the July 13 surrender is a sequel, not a separate engagement record.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 346 (US 46; CS 300); the live field reads 162 (US 74; CS 88). Nicolay quotes Rosecrans: twelve killed and forty-nine wounded, 135 Confederate burials and about twenty wounded, and twenty-one prisoners and two guns taken. Pegram gives his own loss as two officers and 40-45 men killed and about twenty men and four officers wounded, De Lagnel missing, and the enemy's at least thirty killed and forty wounded. His surrendered force was twenty-two officers and 359 men of Heck's regiment and eight officers and 166 men of his own.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The July 13 surrender counts are a later population and are not added to battle casualties.

open_questions: McClellan's July 6-15 reports (No. 2), Rosecrans's Rich Mountain report (No. 5), the Confederate Heck, Tyler, Hotchkiss and Lee Battery reports and the July 8 strength returns of Garnett's and Wise's commands (Nos. 33-34) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. John G. Nicolay's The Outbreak of Rebellion (Scribner, 1881) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, largely from the Official War Records for 1861; it is not independent of the report families. Pegram's July 14 report and July 15 addendum (Official Records Series I, Volume II) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
